name: six-face-spaced-run
description: The DEFAULT six-face run, T-019's best-measured reflex policy: six-face-aimed-run.json plus the two clauses this task's per-tick forensics justified. (1) PERSONAL SPACE — step away from the nearest body when it is inside 2.2 tiles, because the shipped policy's most common damage event is walking or hopping into a CRUISING hostile, not being dived on (a low-lane wasp bobs down to 1.7 above its deck, exactly a standing RIG's head). (2) DON'T POGO AGAINST SOMETHING THAT ISN'T A STEP — `pinned` reports 'jammed while trying to run' without saying why, so answering every pin with a jump makes RIG bounce against the screen's own right clamp, which during a gate sits at the corner pivot; `terrain.stepUp>0.5` makes the jump answer an actual step. MEASURED, NOT ASPIRATIONAL (2026-08-01, `main` pinned and served — the last run from the task/T-019 worktree, whose src/ is byte-identical to main — --deterministic --stop-on-game-over --max-runtime-ms 145000, 1440x900, 9 runs — every one ended at GAME_OVER long before the window): survives 50.2-55.1 s (median 53.1 over all nine; 53.6 over the seven in the finding's own table) against the shipped aimed policy's 46.2-52.8 s (median 48.7 over 8 default-rate runs, re-measured on main by this task — its own file carries both that measurement and T-018's older, unreproduced gate-3 one), 10-16 kills, and reaches wave gate 2 / scroll 140 of 415 EVERY time without clearing it. It does NOT reach VICTORY and no bot run has: the wall, the arithmetic behind it, and the operator packet that has to answer the delivery box are in docs/playtests/2026-08-victory-box.md. Read that before writing another full-run policy. Run-to-run spread is +/-6 s, so read the gate reached, never one run's decimals. (3) CHANGED BY T-027 (I-028): the personal-space clause's guard is `edgeMargin>8`, not the `>6` every measurement above was taken with. The crush-plane emergency (`edgeMargin<8` -> hold right) owns everything below 8; `hold` rules OR per key code, so an overlapping `hold left` there put BOTH direction keys down and computeAim's h=0 left RIG standing still inside the one window whose rule exists to make it run. Re-measured by replaying the three committed T-019 traces through both rule sets (`node analyze-run.mjs <run> --policy <script>` — same trace both ways, so the difference is the guard and nothing else): that pair cancelled on 3/777, 0/717 and 19/501 PLAYING ticks before, and 0/777, 0/717, 0/501 after; all-cause cancellation 5.3/4.5/8.4% -> 4.9/4.5/4.8% of PLAYING ticks. STILL OPEN in the same window, deliberately not touched here: the two gate-servo `hold left` clauses (rules 2 and 4) carry no margin guard at all and still cancel the crush rule on 1, 0 and 7 ticks of those traces. THE TIMING BAND ABOVE HAS NOT BEEN RE-MEASURED with this guard — T-027 ran the changed script twice as a smoke test (42.1 s / 55.8 s, scroll 111 / 140, 7 / 10 kills, both ending at GAME_OVER), which is two runs against a nine-run band and settles nothing. Treat 50.2-55.1 s as the pre-change number until someone re-runs the nine.
